fullData.title: Skip-Counting by Threes on a Number Line
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Emma is counting by threes to find out how many buttons she has. She has 4 groups with 3 buttons in each group. Use the number line to jump by threes 4 times starting from 0 to find the total number of buttons.

fullData.solutionStrategy: Skip-count forward by threes on the number line four times to find the total.

content.altText: A number line from 0 to 12 showing four jumps of plus 3, landing at 3, 6, 9, and 12.

labels.description: Begin your counting journey at zero.
Each jump moves forward by 3 buttons.

annotations.steps: I make four jumps of size three starting from zero on the number line.
annotations.strategy: I notice that jumping by the same size repeatedly helps me add equal groups quickly.
annotations.misconceptions: Starting the first jump at 1 instead of 0 will shift all landing numbers incorrectly.
annotations.connections: Skip-counting on a number line connects repeated addition directly to multiplication.
annotations.narrative: Start at tick $0$ on the number line and jump forward by $3$ four times, landing on ticks $3$, $6$, $9$, and $12$.

steps.title: Calculate the total number of buttons

transitions.operation: multiply groups by buttons in each group

annotations.steps: I multiplied the 4 jumps by 3 buttons each to find the final landing point of 12.
annotations.strategy: I notice that jumping by threes four times is the exact same as multiplying 4 times 3.
annotations.misconceptions: A common mistake is counting the tick marks instead of the spaces or jumps between them.
annotations.connections: This connects skip-counting on a number line directly to multiplication facts.
annotations.narrative: The fourth jump lands on tick $12$, so Emma has a total of $12$ buttons ($4 \times 3 = 12$).

assignment.prompt: Starting at 0 on the number line, what number will Emma land on after making 4 jumps of 3?
assignment.rationale: Starting at 0 and skip-counting by 3 four times lands on 12 (3, 6, 9, 12); starting at 1 shifts the count to 13, making only 3 jumps stops at 9, and adding 4 + 3 gives 7.
